name: tancho_v3_hop_r3

onnx.obs_normalization: inside the model: feed the scaled raw values below, do not normalize again
onnx.action_clip: not inside the model: clip to [-1,1] yourself
onnx.verified: onnxruntime vs TorchScript on reference_io.json: max abs err 9e-8

initial_state.note: tires on z=0 at the default leg pose; spawn ~1 mm higher

observation.name: velocity_command
observation.content: vx m/s, vy (always 0), yaw rate rad/s

observation.name: last_action
observation.content: previous clipped action (6 dims), WITHOUT the reference offsets

observation.name: trigger_LT_RT
observation.content: 0/1 held (LT = lift left leg, RT = right, both = hop)

observation.name: phase_L_R
observation.content: min(seconds since that side's lift started, 0.6) / 0.6; 1 when idle (phase starts at 10 s)

imu_mount.note: +90 deg about x: IMU x = body forward, y = up, z = body right; upright gravity reads (0,-1,0), pitch rate on z

legs.target_rad: default + 0.6 * a + reference_offset(phase of that side)

legs_DM-J4310.type: PD position (Isaac Lab implicit actuator, evaluated every 5 ms physics step)
legs_DM-J4310.torque: tau = 20*(q_target - q) + 0.2*(0 - qdot), clamped to +/-12.5 Nm; PhysX also caps the joint speed at 12.5 rad/s

reference_lift.table: reference_lift_table.csv (per side, 0.02 s steps; offset 0 once phase >= 0.4 s)
press_rules: rising edge while phase[s] < 0.399: queue it (max one), start when that side is free
LT+RT: if both sides want to start but one is still busy, both wait and start together

physics.friction: Isaac: ground 0.8 x robot 0.8 (multiply) = 0.64 effective; MuJoCo combines with max, so set the tire/ground pair to about 0.64
physics.tire_collision: URDF wheel collision geometry, radius 0.03614 m

isaac_results.flat_0.3m_s: LT/RT/LT+RT x2, no fall; one-leg lift 40-45 mm; hop: both tires 33-36 mm, 0.1 s airborne, root +12.8 mm
isaac_results.standing_hops: 5 hops at 0 m/s, no fall, root +12.8 mm

known_gap: DM-J4310 V1.2 TN curve: at 120 rpm only ~4.5 Nm is available; the sim allows 12.5 Nm up to 12.5 rad/s, so it is optimistic for fast leg motions
